newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thai plans extra Paris freighter flight.
newsitem.headline: Thai plans extra Paris freighter flight.

text.p: Thai Airways said it was planning to introduce an additional weekly Boeing 747 freighter frequency between Paris and Bangkok at the end of the month.

"This is very much a last-minute decision in that Thai has a spare freighter on its hands and we are around 90 percent certain it will be deployed on the Paris route," a Paris-based Thai cargo official told Reuters.
Thai already runs a twice-weekly Paris-Bangkok 747F service in conjunction with Air France and also transports freight in the bellyhold of a daily passenger service on the route.

"Last Autumn, under similar circumstances, we introduced an additional freighter on the route for a limited period and this co-incided with a surge in demand and the extra capacity was fully-utilised. Hopefully it will be the same this time round. Cargo load factors are already good at present," the official said.
A mooted Tuesday departure from CDG for the flight would not be optimal in terms of French shippers production cycles but would provide a useful midweek option for spot shipments, the official added.

"The flight's timetabling will probably be more suited to shipments coming from our off-line cargo stations, notably in Spain, where Madrid and Barcelona are generating a good level of business and also for westbound shipments from Asia to Europe," the official added.
The extra freighter frequency will be operated independently of Air France and is scheduled to operate until end-October 1997.
Thai increased its ex-Paris cargo rates by around five percent, effective March 1. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
